text: World Children's Day 2026 - UNICEF and State Securities Commission ring the bell for children's rights at Hanoi Stock Exchange
UNICEF Vietnam, the State Securities Commission of Vietnam (SSC), and the Hanoi Stock Exchange (HNX) today co-organized "Ring the Bell for World Children's Day 2026", with the theme "My Day.

Part of a global campaign led by the United Nations Sustainable Stock Exchanges (UN SSE) and UNICEF, the event highlighted the critical role of capital markets and the private sector in advancing children's rights and shaping a more sustainable future.
Children make up nearly one-third of the world's population, yet their rights and interests remain largely invisible in many business and investment decisions.

From the products and services designed for them and the marketing they are exposed to, to their parents' working conditions, supply chains, and the environmental impact of business operations, corporate decisions can profoundly shape children's lives - often without children ever being considered in the process.

Bringing together regulators, listed companies, investors, and young people, the event underscored a shared commitment to making children ' s rights and well-being integral to responsible business and investment decisions.

The program culminated in the symbolic ringing of the opening bell at the Hanoi Stock Exchange at 9am - reinforcing a powerful message: investing in children is not just an investment in their future, but in the future of Vietnam's economy and society .
"A truly mature capital market must develop with depth, quality, and a long-term perspective," said Mr. Ha Duy Tung, Vice Chairman of the SSC.
"Children's rights are not peripheral to business; they are closely linked to corporate governance, risk management, and companies' long-term, sustainable development.

Through this event, I hope to strengthen dialogue among regulators, businesses, investors, UNICEF, and other partners, and encourage greater attention to children and future generations in business and investment decisions.

"The bell we ring today is a call to recognize children as a distinct stakeholder group, to connect sustainable finance with sustainable futures, and to ensure that growth creates opportunity for every child," said Ms. Michaela Bauer, Representative (Officer-in-Charge), at UNICEF Vietnam.
"When children are healthier, safer, better educated, and prepared for the future, societies prosper, markets become more resilient, and businesses are better placed to grow.
The campaign coincides with the forthcoming launch of the UN SSE's Model Guidance on Applying a Child Lens to Business and Investor Practices , developed in partnership with UNICEF.

It offers practical recommendations and training for stock exchanges and their listed companies on identifying, managing, and disclosing child-related impacts, risks, and opportunities across governance, strategy, operations, and value chains.
As part of World Children's Day celebrations in Vietnam, UNICEF is also inviting children and young people to submit short videos sharing their perspectives on their rights and the future they want.
The initiative creates space for children to express themselves in their own words and helps bring their voices into public conversations about the decisions shaping their lives and communities.
